**Instructions.** Choose the single best answer (a–e) for each question. You may use a periodic table.
Calculators are allowed. Answers are rounded to the precision shown. Time yourself: aim for about 30 minutes
(roughly 2 minutes per question, the same pace as the full exam). **Solubility rules are not provided:** work from memory, as on the exam.

**Answer sheet.** Use the bubble answer sheet (`CHEM1301/exam-prep/answer-sheet/answer-sheet.pdf`), rows 1–15.

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**1.** Which best describes an aqueous solution of barium nitrate, Ba(NO~3~)~2~(aq)?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Separated Ba^2+^ and NO~3~^−^ ions, with two NO~3~^−^ ions for every Ba^2+^ ion, moving independently\
b)\ Intact Ba(NO~3~)~2~ units dissolved in water\
c)\ Ba atoms and NO~3~ molecules with no charge\
d)\ A solid suspended in water, because barium salts are insoluble\
e)\ Separated Ba^2+^ and NO~3~^−^ ions in a 1 : 1 ratio

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

**4.** Which solubility rule explains why (NH~4~)~2~CO~3~ is **soluble** in water?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Rule 4: most sulfates are soluble, except BaSO~4~, PbSO~4~, and CaSO~4~\
b)\ Rule 1: most nitrate (NO~3~^−^) salts are soluble\
c)\ Rule 6: most sulfides, carbonates, and phosphates are only slightly soluble\
d)\ Rule 5: most hydroxides are only slightly soluble (NaOH and KOH are the exceptions)\
e)\ Rule 2: most salts of Na^+^, K^+^, and NH~4~^+^ are soluble

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**5.** Which solubility rule explains why BaSO~4~ is **insoluble** in water?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Rule 4: most sulfates are soluble, except BaSO~4~, PbSO~4~, and CaSO~4~\
b)\ Rule 6: most sulfides, carbonates, and phosphates are only slightly soluble\
c)\ Rule 2: most salts of Na^+^, K^+^, and NH~4~^+^ are soluble\
d)\ Rule 1: most nitrate (NO~3~^−^) salts are soluble\
e)\ Rule 3: most chlorides are soluble, except AgCl, PbCl~2~, and Hg~2~Cl~2~

**9.** Which is the balanced **molecular** equation for mixing aqueous MgCl~2~ and K~3~PO~4~?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 3MgCl~2~(aq) + 2K~3~PO~4~(aq) $\rightarrow$ Mg~3~(PO~4~)~2~(aq) + 6KCl(s)\
b)\ MgCl~2~(aq) + K~3~PO~4~(aq) $\rightarrow$ MgPO~4~(s) + KCl(aq)\
c)\ No reaction (NR)\
d)\ MgCl~2~(aq) + K~3~PO~4~(aq) $\rightarrow$ Mg~3~(PO~4~)~2~(s) + KCl(aq)\
e)\ 3MgCl~2~(aq) + 2K~3~PO~4~(aq) $\rightarrow$ Mg~3~(PO~4~)~2~(s) + 6KCl(aq)

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

\needspace{9\baselineskip}

**12.** Aqueous solutions of lead(II) nitrate and potassium chloride are mixed. What is the **net ionic** equation?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Pb^2+^(aq) + 2Cl^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ PbCl~2~(s)\
b)\ Pb^2+^(aq) + Cl^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ PbCl~2~(s)\
c)\ Pb^2+^(aq) + 2NO~3~^−^(aq) + 2K^+^(aq) + 2Cl^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ PbCl~2~(s) + 2K^+^(aq) + 2NO~3~^−^(aq)\
d)\ K^+^(aq) + NO~3~^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ KNO~3~(s)\
e)\ No reaction occurs (NR)

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

**15.** In a precipitation reaction, **spectator ions** are ions that:

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ appear only in the net ionic equation\
b)\ are always Na^+^ and NO~3~^−^\
c)\ combine to form the precipitate\
d)\ change their charge during the reaction\
e)\ are present in solution but do not participate directly in the reaction, so they are left out of the net ionic equation

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```
